title: Search bias, baselines and robustness
objectives: Explain why optimizing a noisy validation score selects noise, and evaluate a frozen choice against later held-out/baseline evidence under matched assumptions.
Compute a bounded exact one-sided fair-sign null p-value and fixed-family Bonferroni adjustment, stating marginal null validity, trial-family and dependence/market limits.
Apply search bias, baselines and robustness invariants safely and identify scope boundaries.
motivation: Searching thresholds, features, seeds, universes, dates, execution/cost assumptions and stopping times can fit noise even when the final model has few parameters. Reporting only the best score hides the search.

blocks.md: Searching thresholds, features, seeds, universes, dates, execution/cost assumptions and stopping times can fit noise even when the final model has few parameters. Reporting only the best score hides the search. Cawley/Talbot document that overfitting the selection criterion can materially bias evaluation. A validation score used to choose a candidate is a selection score, not independent performance evidence for the winner.

Own synthetic validation means: A 5, B 6, cash 0 bps. Choose B using validation only, with deterministic lexical tie rule. Later holdout means: A -2, B -4, cash 0. Report B validation 6 and later -4 alongside cash 0, not a silent switch to the holdout winner cash. This one example illustrates a possible selection failure; it does not estimate how often failures happen or prove every selected model loses. A valid strategy can also underperform over a short holdout.

blocks.title: One impressive trial versus a declared family
items: Under an explicitly iid fair-sign null, eight independent +1 signs have one-sided tail probability 1/256. The statistic counts positive signs; it ignores economic magnitudes and costs.
If this is one of a fixed family of 20 valid marginal tests, Bonferroni adjusted p=min(1,20/256)=5/64≈0.078125. At predeclared alpha 0.05, the raw test rejects but the adjusted family test does not.

Union bound: if each true-null test has P(p_i<=alpha/m)<=alpha/m, then probability of any false rejection<=sum(alpha/m)<=alpha. Tests need not be independent from each other, but their marginal p-values and the declared finite family must be valid. This does not repair invalid time-series sign assumptions or hidden/adaptive trials.

blocks.caption: Expected 1/256 5/64 True False; B 6 -4; invalid fair-sign sample. Complete exact Fraction/binomial tail source, not estimated Monte Carlo p. Family size supplied by caller must match actual predefined comparisons;code cannot discover omitted trials, validate iid market signs or correct arbitrary adaptive experimentation. No t-test/Sharpe significance or real trading returns inferred.

blocks.md: A p-value is a null-tail probability for a specified statistic/protocol, not the probability the strategy is false or a guarantee a rejection will profit. The fair-sign model assumes independent signs, each equally likely positive/negative under the null, with no zeros here. Market returns may be dependent/asymmetric, net of costs and continuous magnitudes;converting them blindly to this toy p-value is unjustified. Failure to reject does not establish no effect, and significance does not establish economic relevance.

Compare against an appropriate no-trade/cash, passive or simple strategy baseline with matched universe, timing, exposure/currency, data, cost/financing and evaluation interval. A high gross return from leverage or omitted costs is not automatically excess skill. Predeclare economic metrics, drawdown/turnover/liquidity exposure and acceptable failure modes, then show tradeoff/sensitivity rather than only a winning Sharpe. Cash baseline return is 0 ONLY in this declared zero-interest synthetic example.

Perturb defensible assumptions within an a-priori grid: costs/delays, capacity, periods, universes and nearby parameter values. Report the whole surface and failure regions, including valid runs with poor outcomes. Repeated robustness exploration becomes more search; do not relabel only favorable perturbations as confirmation. Costs can alter path and lower fills can avoid losses, so empirical responses need interpretation rather than a universal monotonic slogan.

Nested evaluation fits/chooses the full procedure within each inner training/validation loop, and evaluates it on outer held-out data. sklearn's Iris example explains the selection principle but uses shuffled classification folds;do NOT copy that splitting into historical market forecasting. Use time/label-aware inner AND outer boundaries and train-only preprocessing from the prior lesson. Nested evaluation estimates the tested procedure under its data assumptions, not tomorrow's regime or a cure for every hidden human research choice.

Independent transfer: enumerate all 2^n sign sequences for small n and check the exact tail count/p-value superuniform property under the stated fair null. Compare raw and fixed-family adjustment at predeclared alpha, then explain why unrecorded/adaptive trials break the given accounting. Freeze a candidate before reading a separate holdout, compare a same-rules baseline, and publish failures as well as scores. No positive result is a professional/trading competence certificate.

Sources: [Cawley/Talbot 2010 original model-selection-bias paper page](http://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html), [sklearn nested selection principle, Iris not market folds](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/model_selection/plot_nested_cross_validation_iris.html), [NIST Bonferroni general inequality](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/prc/section4/prc473.htm). Fair-sign exact tail and fixed-family p-adjustment are derived here from binomial counting/union bound, not a new market inference method.

guidedExercise.prompt: Why is a tiny adjusted p-value plus a favorable cost sensitivity grid insufficient to approve live trading?
hints: Checks inference and search protocol limits.
Requires independent scoped evidence and operational review.
guidedExercise.solution: Null/marginal assumptions and complete fixed trial family may fail; adaptive choices/hidden trials/temporal leakage can remain. Significance is not economic relevance or risk/liquidity capacity. Need independently held-out procedure/baseline/outcomes, realistic data/cost/execution and risk/operational/authority review. No future profit or competence guarantee.

independentExercise.prompt: Write a small test case that deliberately breaks the contract boundary in "Search bias, baselines and robustness" and verify how your implementation rejects or handles it.
hints: Test zero, negative, empty, duplicate, and boundary values.
Confirm both time/memory complexity and numerical precision remain within spec.

commonMistakes: Selection is part of fitting the research procedure. (Evaluate the frozen procedure on later held-out data.)
Do not confuse within-test null assumptions with cross-test dependence. (Union bound holds without cross-test independence.)
(10+2)/2=6 bps; that score was used for selection.
realWorldApplication: In practice, engineering teams apply search bias, baselines and robustness within Research Infrastructure and Backtesting when building reliable backtesting and quant modelling workflows — specifically to explain why optimizing a noisy validation score selects noise, and evaluate a frozen choice against later held-out/baseline evidence under matched assumptions.
quantFinanceApplication: Desk workflows in Research Infrastructure and Backtesting rely on search bias, baselines and robustness across backtesting, quant modelling, data infrastructure, keeping numerical estimates, risk bounds, and low-latency paths predictable.
summary: Selection searches can overfit validation noise; freeze choices and report later matched-baseline evidence honestly.
Exact toy fair-sign/Bonferroni arithmetic needs valid null marginals and a declared family, not hidden adaptive trials.
Robustness/nested time-aware evaluation remain scoped, not future-profit guarantees.

quiz.prompt: After selecting B because it wins validation, what is its validation score?
options: An unbiased estimate of the selected winner because each candidate score was unbiased before selection
quiz.explanation: Selection is part of fitting the research procedure. (Evaluate the frozen procedure on later held-out data.)

quiz.prompt: What does Bonferroni NOT require across tests when marginal p-values/family are valid?
quiz.explanation: Do not confuse within-test null assumptions with cross-test dependence. (Union bound holds without cross-test independence.)

quiz.prompt: B validation returns 10 and 2 bps have what mean?
quiz.explanation: (10+2)/2=6 bps; that score was used for selection.

quiz.prompt: The later holdout favors cash over the validation-selected B. What is honest?
options: Report B held-out result and baseline comparison
Replace B with cash and call the same holdout unseen
Delete the holdout as a bad period
Claim all strategies are proven useless
quiz.explanation: Keep the tested selection protocol visible. (Switching choices uses the holdout for selection.)

quiz.prompt: Can the shuffled Iris nested-CV example be copied unchanged for market forecasting?
options: Yes, because nested removes every leakage path
Only if the test winner is profitable
No, use time-aware inner and outer splits
quiz.explanation: Carry temporal availability contracts into the full evaluation procedure. (The principle transfers, not arbitrary shuffled folds.)
